summary: Frank Lee Woodward was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College under Caroline Rhys Davids, he served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society (around 1914–1919).

Frank Raymond Allchin specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at SOAS and the University of London under K. de B. Codrington, then held posts at SOAS (1954–1959), Cambridge (1959–1989), and the Ancient India and Iran Trust (around 1978–2010).

Frank-Richard Hamm worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and at the International Academy of Indian Culture, he held posts at Hamburg (1948–1952, 1957–1964) and became a professor at Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Hermann Collitz, he served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (around 1921–1928), where he also worked (around 1928–1937), followed by posts at Halle-Wittenberg (around 1937–1950) and Free University of Berlin (around 1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He is attested as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles, from 2002 to 2006.

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen, completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt, and served as professor at the University of Hamburg from 1966 to 1971.

Franz Boas was a scholar in linguistics and anthropology who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held positions at Clark University, the Smithsonian Institution, the American Museum of Natural History (1896–1900), and Columbia University (around 1896–1936).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard Chézy, and at London and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.
Franz Ferdinand Schwarz was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Graz from 1953 to 1958 and later served as a professor there from around 1974 to 1999.

Franz Heinrich Trithen specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, later holding positions at the British Museum (around 1844–1848) and the University of Oxford (around 1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen, where he assumed the chair in Indology in 1881.

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, he was appointed lecturer in oriental languages (1829) and extraordinary professor of theology (1831) at Berlin.
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and his Ph.D. from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Rostock from around 1810 to 1814, he held a post at Kazan Imperial University from around 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and held a professorship at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who has held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2003).
François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon from around 1951 to 1956. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who has served as a professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2008 and 2013.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian educated at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts as Director of Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine (around 2001) and Director of Research at the CNRS (appointed 2002).
